source: DHM Islamic Studies Level 2 · lesson 19. Exercises reused from the lesson.
topic: As-Sadiq, Al-Ameen: the truthful, the trustworthy

learn.en: At twelve he could not bear to be apart from his uncle, so Abu Talib took him on the caravan to Syria. In Busra a monk recognised him as the Last Prophet.
learn.title: The journey to Syria

learn.en: Allah protected him as he grew up. He stayed away from every bad habit and was the bravest, most truthful and most trustworthy.
learn.title: Protected by Allah

learn.en: As a young man he became a trader. Because he was honest, hardworking and kind, people called him As-Sadiq and Al-Ameen.
learn.title: As-Sadiq, Al-Ameen

learn.en: Once a man asked him to wait until he came back to finish a deal — and forgot. Three days later he found the Prophet ﷺ still waiting at the same spot!
learn.title: Still waiting

learn.en: “And indeed, you are of a great moral character.” (Qur'an 68:4)
learn.title: From the Qur'an

quiz.en: How old was he when he went to Syria with Abu Talib?
Where did the monk recognise him?
After how many days did the man come back?
True or false? The Prophet ﷺ became a trader as a young man.

think.q: The Prophet ﷺ kept his promise even when it was hard. Is there a promise you need to keep this week?
think.a: Keeping promises makes people trust you — like Al-Ameen ﷺ.

parents.summary: The trip to Syria, Allah's protection in his youth, and honest trade that earned him the names As-Sādiq and Al-Amīn.
parents.tip: Praise him whenever he keeps a promise: “That's Al-Ameen behaviour!”
